newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen rising after PPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen rising after PPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open higher on Friday after a report on the June Producer Price Index, market analysts said. The following are their comments:
ROY BLUMBERG, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST JOSEPHTHAL LYON & ROSS
-- "There's going to be a small positive reaction to it."

-- "There's no fear out there among investors. There's still the belief you buy every dip. If you get a slightly better-than-expected piece of economic news, than you would expect them to continue that buying process."

The Labor Department reported the June PPI fell 0.1 percent and the core rate, excluding food and energy components, rose 0.1 percent. Economists in a Reuter poll had expected, on average, for the June PPI to be unchanged, with the core rising 0.1 percent.
ALAN ACKERMAN, MARKET STRATEGIST, FAHNESTOCK AND CO:

-- "Inflation is certainly not sending scary signals. The inflation price index fell again, for the sixth month in a row. As a results, look for a lift in stocks and bonds. The 8,000 level on the Dow is likely to be challenged soon, and today's market should help those expectations."
PETER CARDILLO, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH, WESTFALIA INVESTMENTS:
-- "These are good numbers which show inflation is going nowhere, particularly at the producer level. Bonds are up and I look for a higher opening for stocks."

-- "Crude goods were down, intermediate goods were unchanged, and food prices were down. This is the key because crude goods and food are the volatile sectors of the component which could make inflation do funny things.
-- "I suspect we are headed for a higher open and I would not be surprised to see the market close above 8,000 today."
The 30-year Treasury bond was unchanged, yielding 6.56 percent.
The S&P 500 future was flat at 921.50.
ISABEL CABRAL, FINCOR
"For me, and I think for all, it was a surprise. I think it has to do with the conviction that inflation will renew its downward trend in June."
ANA PAULA CARVALHO, BANCO PORTUGUES DE INVESTIMENTO
"We were expecting a cut...so it does not surprise. There is space for further cuts even if not in the short term."
JOAO LOURENCO, SIEMCA
"Taking account of the significant economic growth, there could still be some adjustment to come, but right now, based on current conditions, the room for further falls seems to be almost exhausted."
--Lisbon bureau 3511-3150035
